text:
Assumption had 2 licensed child care facilities in 2025, state data shows
In 2025, Assumption was home to two licensed child care facilities, as reported by the Illinois Department of Children and Family Services.
Among these facilities, one held a license as a day care center (50%) and the other was a group day care home (50%).
These Assumption providers served children from birth to 12 years and from 6 weeks to 5 years of age.
All child care providers in Assumption offered services in English.
Across Illinois, there were 8,602 licensed child care facilities in 2025.
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has frozen certain federal child care and family assistance grants for California, Colorado, Minnesota, New York and Illinois amid concerns over fraud and misuse, the agency announced Jan. 6. The freeze impacts nearly $2.4 billion in Child Care and Development Fund grants, $7.35 billion in Temporary Assistance for Needy Families funds and $869 million in Social Services Block Grants. States must provide sufficient documentation before payments are processed.
Gov. J.B. Pritzker of Illinois called the decision “wrong and cruel” and said Illinois could contest the freeze, noting that anti‑fraud procedures are already in effect in the state.
The Illinois administration estimates the freeze could impact about 100,000 families and more than 152,000 children using the state’s Child Care Assistance Program, as well as thousands of licensed providers and 275 human services organizations.
